pattern.crimePattern: a wife strikes her husband with her crystal award as he leaves her, then plants his watch, money and the award on the nanny, whose own baby monitor proves where she was
pattern.notes: Fictional family, agency and compound. PLANTED with two planted items (the award and the money), so the second is an accepted alternative. The nanny everyone is ready to blame is the witness who clears herself, on the nursery camera.

facts.text: Jeff Gitau was found dead at the foot of the stairs of his Lavington maisonette on Sunday morning; his wife says the nanny stole his watch and money. His brother Tom is at a wedding in Naivasha.
A head wound and fall injuries. His packed weekend bag at the top of the stairs. No forced door or window.
Nduku: "I slept through everything. In the morning I found him. His watch and the money in his bag are gone. The nanny's been strange for weeks."
In Nekesa's handbag in the kitchen: Jeff's watch and KSh 80,000 in a bank envelope.
Under Nekesa's bed: Nduku's heavy crystal PR award, wiped, chipped on one corner.
Under the award, the floor's layer of dust is undisturbed beneath its base; the award's top is clean.
Anything that has lain under a bed for weeks gathers dust on top and protects the floor beneath it.
Jeff's phone: Sheila, 22:50, "Taxi booked for you at 11:15." Jeff, 22:52, "Packing now. Telling her."
Baby monitor audio: a man and a woman shouting in the hallway 23:05–23:08 ("You're not taking that bag anywhere!"), then a heavy thud and a crash at 23:08.
Baby monitor video: Nekesa in the nursery, in frame, 22:48–23:44, rocking and singing to the baby. At the crash she freezes and stays.
Nekesa: "I heard shouting and a crash. Madam came to the nursery door at half past eleven and said, 'Stay with the baby, it's nothing, Jeff dropped his bag.' I was afraid. I stayed."
Saidi: "Bwana Jeff told me at nine he'd be leaving with a bag around eleven. His car never left."
Saidi was at the gate all night (gate camera).
Visitors' book: a taxi for J. Gitau waited outside from 23:12 and left with no passenger at 23:40. No other visitor after 21:00.
Records ②: Nduku called her sister Mwikali at 23:30 for 14 minutes. At 23:20 Sheila rang Jeff's phone; nobody answered.
Tom was at a family wedding in Naivasha, Friday to Sunday.
Mwikali's phone was at her home in Machakos all night; the call came to her there.
Sheila's phone was at her flat in Kilimani all night, and she never came to the compound.
Tom: "Jeff told me on Friday he was leaving her. He was afraid of how she'd take it."
Fingerprints taken from Nduku in detention.
Post-mortem: one blow to the temple from a sharp-edged heavy object, then the fall injuries.
Post-mortem: death on Saturday between 23:00 and 23:30.
Lab: Jeff's blood in the award's chipped corner, though the rest was wiped.
Lab: Nduku's prints on the bank envelope and the watch strap. None of Nekesa's.
Missing: there's no dust on top of the award, and none disturbed beneath it.
Nduku: "I slept through everything."
Nduku: "The nanny stole from us."
Nduku: "He packed a bag in front of me and said the house was his company's. Twenty years. I don't remember picking up the award." Advocate Gachoki: "Nothing further."
Nduku: "I never touched his money or his watch."
Mwikali: "Nduku didn't call me that night."
Mwikali: "She called at half eleven crying. She said, 'Jeff fell. I've done something terrible. I'll handle it.' I told her to call the police. She said no."
Sheila: "Jeff wasn't coming to me. We'd ended it."
Sheila: "He was coming. I booked the taxi. I waited until two. I thought he'd changed his mind."
Nekesa: "I never took anything. I was with the baby."
Nekesa: "I'm from Bungoma. If they say a nanny stole, who'll believe me?"
Tom: "I was in Naivasha."

reconstruction.text: On Saturday evening Jeff tells Nduku he is leaving her for Sheila, that he will file for divorce on Monday, and that the house is in his company's name. At nine he tells the guard he'll leave with a bag at eleven.

At 22:52 he texts Sheila: "Packing now. Telling her." At 23:05 he comes out of the bedroom with his bag; Nduku follows him to the top of the stairs. They shout. At 23:08 she strikes him with her crystal award and he falls.

Nekesa, in the nursery with the baby, freezes. Nduku takes the watch and KSh 80,000 from his bag and pushes them into Nekesa's handbag, wipes the award and slides it under Nekesa's bed. At 23:30 she calls her sister, crying.
At 23:40 the taxi leaves without him. At 06:15 Nduku "finds" him and tells the police the nanny did it in a robbery.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: the baby-monitor cloud (which also reopens Nduku) and her phone records. The award's blood trace (12 h) goes first thing; detain Nduku after the calls, and the prints (6 h) come back inside 24 h.
